# Altair/Vega-Lite Python Code for Seattle Weather

Here's a simple example to get started:

```python
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
url = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/altair-viz/vega_datasets/master/data/seattle-weather.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(url)

# Simple bar chart of weather conditions
chart = alt.Chart(data).mark_bar().encode(
    x='weather:N',
    y='count()'
).properties(
    width=400,
    height=300,
    title='Seattle Weather Conditions'
).interactive()

chart.show()
```

## More Advanced Examples

**Temperature over time:**
```python
chart = alt.Chart(data).mark_line().encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='temp_max:Q',
    color='weather:N'
).properties(
    width=800,
    height=400,
    title='Seattle Max Temperature Over Time'
).interactive()

chart.show()
```

**Precipitation vs Temperature scatter:**
```python
chart = alt.Chart(data).mark_point().encode(
    x='temp_max:Q',
    y='precipitation:Q',
    color='weather:N',
    size='wind:Q'
).properties(
    width=500,
    height=400,
    title='Precipitation vs Temperature'
).interactive()

chart.show()
```

The dataset includes: `date`, `precipitation`, `temp_max`, `temp_min`, `wind`, and `weather` (condition type).
